title: dispatch --resume --detach prints a wait that starts before the resumed worker's own working event when its process is slow to post it
goal: the wait that dispatch --resume --detach prints starts at or after the resumed worker's own working event, though its detached process is slow to post it

run:
import os,subprocess,sys,tempfile,time,io,contextlib,argparse,signal
T=os.path.abspath("_tools")
d=tempfile.mkdtemp(); os.environ["KB_COORD_STORE"]=d+"/s.sqlite"
sys.path.insert(0,T); import bl_dispatch as D, bl_clean
from pathlib import Path
iid="ST-aaaaaaaa"
class BL:
    root=d
    def label(self,i): return i
def spawn(bl,a,i,scratch):  # a resume: its work branch exists, its detached process posts `working` 12 s after it starts
    argv=["sh","-c","sleep 12; "+sys.executable+" "+T+"/coord.py post --kind progress --field item="+i+" --field state=working >/dev/null; sleep 5"]
    return subprocess.Popen(argv),Path(d)/"log"
D.spawn_detached=spawn; D.begin_wait=lambda bl,i,pid: True
buf=io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buf): D.start_detached(BL(),argparse.Namespace(resume=iid),iid,Path(d))
since=int(buf.getvalue().split("--since ")[1].split()[0]); time.sleep(13)
_,body,_=bl_clean.run_coord("wait","--since","0","--timeout","0")
seq=[e["seq"] for e in body["events"] if e["fields"].get("state")=="working"]
print("printed --since",since,"; the resumed worker own working event is seq",seq)
sys.exit(0 if seq and since>=max(seq) else 1)
